protocol.description:
This protocol allows a client to register triggerable actions, a.k.a. shortcuts.
A client can request a shortcut and the compositor decides which key combination, if any, triggers it. Triggering a shortcut does not move keyboard focus to the client, which is the point: a client can act on a key press without the window underneath losing activation.

interface.name: hyprland_global_shortcuts_manager_v1
interface.description: This object is a manager for registering global shortcuts.

entry.name: already_taken
entry.summary: the combination of app_id and id is already taken

request.name: register_shortcut
request.description:
Register a new global shortcut.
A global shortcut is anonymous, meaning the app does not know what key(s) trigger it. The shortcut's keybinding is set by the compositor's configuration.
If the combination of app_id and id is already taken, the compositor raises an already_taken error.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: the shortcut's id, unique within the app

arg.name: trigger_description
arg.summary: user-facing hint at how it is triggered

request.name: destroy
request.description: All objects created by the manager will still remain valid, until their appropriate destroy request has been called.

interface.name: hyprland_global_shortcut_v1
interface.description: This object represents a single shortcut.

arg.name: tv_sec_hi
arg.summary: high 32 bits of the seconds part of the timestamp

arg.name: tv_sec_lo
arg.summary: low 32 bits of the seconds part of the timestamp

arg.name: tv_sec_hi
arg.summary: high 32 bits of the seconds part of the timestamp

arg.name: tv_sec_lo
arg.summary: low 32 bits of the seconds part of the timestamp

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the shortcut. Can be sent at any time by the client.
